chapter_seo_title: Han Li Chooses Small Huan Island – Why He Picks the Weakest Spirit Vein
chapter_meta_description: Han Li skips the best cultivation spots on Starfall Island and picks Small Huan Island, a qi-poor outlier. The bureaucrat laughs, but Han Li’s plan is perfectly clear: the Heaven Vial doesn’t need strong energy.
og_title: Han Li Becomes an Island Lord—On the Worst Island
og_description: He chooses the runt of the map: thin qi, high costs, and a long list of failures before him. But for a man with a secret green bottle, isolation is the real treasure.
twitter_title: Why Han Li Picked the Worst Island on the Map
twitter_description: Every other cultivator fled within years. Han Li signs up on day one. The secret? His Heaven Vial doesn’t need rich spiritual qi—it grows its own.

lore_anchors.definition: A classical Chinese idiom for something that is tasteless to eat yet a pity to discard; in cultivation fiction, it describes a resource or location that is not worth fighting for but too valuable to simply abandon.

A de facto title granted to a cultivator who selects a remote island as their cultivation site, carrying full responsibility for the island’s protective formation costs and tax exemption to the main sect.
The administrative hall on Azure Cloud Mountain where cultivators register for cultivation sites and receive their proof of claim in the form of a jade slip.
Han Li's speed-focused flying artifact, refined from Ink Flood Dragon fin and tail; fast but lacks defensive capabilities.
